scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Tertali, also known as Teratali or Terah Taali, is an elaborate ritual folk dance performed by the Kamar tribes in Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, India.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Tertali is an elaborate ritual containing many different types of dance, performed as part of Kamar tribal tradition.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is generally performed by two or three women sitting on the ground.
Performers tie thirteen manjiras (small metal cymbals) to different parts of their body and strike them rhythmically.
At times, dancers clench a small sword between their teeth and balance an ornamental pot on their head while playing the cymbals.
Watch for Manjira Striking, Head Balancing, Sword Clenching.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Two or three women seated on the ground.
